thesis: A switching-cost information-management franchise with a rising operating margin, a 14.34% FCF yield and shrinking share count trades at the floor of its own 5-year multiples, where the price implies a -13.4% revenue collapse that a 1.7% divestiture-adjusted decline does not show.
reason: The falling direction is limited to FCF margin and is explained by financing and transition costs. Operating margin and ROCE are rising over the last year. At a 14.34% FCF yield the skew is favourable. Organic decline, 3.10x leverage and the February plan keep conviction at 4, not 5. Python sets the standard volatility-scaled core size.

triggers.text: TTM operating margin falls below 20% (23.0% now, 20.5% a year earlier), showing that the margin gains were cost cuts on a shrinking base rather than durable.
TTM FCF margin falls below 13% (16.3% now), turning the explained FCF dip into structural cash erosion from interest and organic decline.
Net debt/EBITDA on the ratios page rises above 3.7x (3.10x TTM now), showing buybacks are outrunning deleveraging.
Total revenue growth after divestiture adjustments is below -4% in two consecutive 10-Qs, or the company withdraws or cuts its full-year outlook, including in the February multi-year plan.

thesis: A net-cash, still-growing contact-centre and AI customer-service software franchise trades below its own 5-year minimum EV/EBITDA and EV/Sales at a 9.16% FCF yield, where the price implies a steep revenue decline that beat-and-raise results do not show, while the rolling margin dip is largely investment, buyback-funded capital deployment and restructuring.
reason: The rolling decline is mostly explained (cash deployed, restructuring, investment) with the balance sheet intact and guidance raised; the price already discounts shrinkage. Falling gross margin and AI seat risk are real, so conviction 4, not 5, at the standard vol-scaled size. Technology stays within the cap once the pending JKHY exit fills.

triggers.text: TTM operating margin falls below 15% (17.2% now), showing the margin fall is not restructuring and investment but lost pricing.
TTM FCF margin falls below 14% (17.6% now), showing cash generation is deteriorating structurally rather than resetting.
TTM gross margin falls below 62% (64.0% now), confirming AI-driven price/mix pressure on the seat-based model.
TTM ROIC falls below 8% (10.2% now), showing the deployed capital is not earning its keep.

thesis: A cash-generative seating and E-Systems supplier with rolling ROIC rising to an 11.4% 2-year high, a 13.19% FCF yield and accretive buybacks trades below every 5-year minimum multiple, where the price implies an -8.4% revenue decline that Q3 growth and held core earnings guidance do not show.
reason: The recent direction is favourable or flat: returns are rising and the FCF slip is small and explained, so the cheapness is a cyclical discount with an intact balance sheet, not structural decay. Thin margins, sector-wide cheapness, China competition and USMCA cap conviction at 4, not 5. Standard volatility-scaled core size.

triggers.text: TTM ROIC falls below 9%, reversing the rolling rise from 9.6% to 11.4% and showing returns are deteriorating.
TTM operating margin falls below 4.0%, close to the FY2022 five-year low of 3.8%, showing OEM pricing or Chinese competition is compressing profitability structurally.
TTM FCF margin falls below 2.0% (2.9% now), showing cash generation can no longer fund the buybacks.
Management cuts full-year core operating earnings guidance, a 10-Q discloses that tariffs or USMCA terms materially reduce gross profit, or net debt/EBITDA on the ratios page rises above 2.0x.

thesis: A fee-based US midstream network with ROIC at its 2-year high, falling leverage and a twice-raised 2026 guide trades at its 5-year minimum EV/EBITDA and below peers, while the margin and FCF dip is explained by inventory build and growth capex rather than a structural decline.
reason: The rolling-12-month fall is a cash-timing and investment effect: ROIC rose, leverage fell and ratings improved. EBITDA-based cheapness against own history and peers gives a positive skew. Conviction capped at 4, standard size, because FCF conversion is weak, Apollo Class B ranks ahead of common and the mechanical bear sits below the price.

triggers.text: TTM operating margin falls below 12% (14.2% now), showing the cost increases are structural rather than an inventory and timing effect.
TTM ROIC falls below 7% (8.8% now), showing the growth capex and Brazos are not earning their cost of capital.
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 4.5x (3.68x now) once Brazos is in the numbers, reversing the deleveraging behind the BBB+ upgrade.
TTM FCF conversion (FCF/NI, cash-flow and income-statement pages) falls below 50% (62.2% now), meaning the NGL inventory build is not reversing into cash.
